subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: Should Codex WebChat keep immediate `chat.send` started ACK semantics, or must it prove native-thread turn startup or rotate/fail before acknowledging the user message?
rationale: Current code intentionally separates WebChat acceptance from native Codex turn execution, and the safest user-visible contract requires maintainer intent before automation changes gateway ACK timing, Codex rotation policy, or recovery behavior.

options.title: Keep open for liveness contract
options.body: Require a maintainer-owned contract and focused proof that accepted sends cannot silently wedge before a durable turn or visible failure.

options.title: Fail or rotate before ACK
options.body: Change Codex/WebChat send handling so native startup pressure is resolved before returning `started`, trading latency for stronger acceptance semantics.

options.title: Preserve immediate ACK with recovery
options.body: Keep fast ACKs but require post-ACK lifecycle errors, user-visible recovery, and transcript audit records for every native startup failure.

recommendation.title: Keep open for liveness contract
recommendation.body: Require a maintainer-owned contract and focused proof that accepted sends cannot silently wedge before a durable turn or visible failure.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the most relevant current Codex startup-binding mitigation and are the clearest owner for deciding whether that guard is sufficient or needs a stronger ACK contract.
